about: Every idea from the weekly GitHub search, from proposal to kept or removed (docs/LEARNING.md, part 3). Test and removal rules are written here BEFORE any test is run and are not changed after seeing results.

ideas.title: Volatility-scaled share of the long-term bucket
ideas.source: pysystemtrade (GPL-3.0, idea only); Moreira & Muir 2017 J. Finance; critique Cederburg et al. 2020 J. Financial Economics
ideas.review: Claims check out. Conflicts with an approved rule: long-term funds are sold only on a measured thesis break, never on price moves; adopting this needs that rule changed first. The proposal had no trading frequency; fixed below. Likely to cut drops and returns together, so it may fail the gain part of the bar.
ideas.where: Backtest first (36-start account test). If it passes and you approve: the main paper account's long-term bucket, the only account with one.
ideas.backtest_rule: Long-term share of what L1 holds = min(1, 15% / SPY 20-day realised volatility, annualised), read at each close. Trade only when the held share is 10 points or more away from it (next open). The rest of the bucket is idle cash (BIL in backtests, as config). 36 quarterly starts Apr 2015 - Jan 2024, 24 months, $300 + $250/month, 40/60: beats today's rules in >= 60% of starts, median gain > 0, median worst drop no more than 1 point deeper; then 2026 must not lose to today's rules by more than 1 point.
ideas.live_check: Every session, the long-term bucket is compared with the same bucket unscaled (same deposits, no scaling).
ideas.removal_rule: After 63 sessions or more: removed if the scaled bucket trails the unscaled one by more than the 5th percentile of same-length gaps in the 2015-2025 backtest. Early removal after 21 sessions if it trails by more than the 1st percentile.

ideas.title: Trailing stop for the 52-week-high breakout (S2)
ideas.source: freqtrade custom_stoploss (GPL-3.0, idea only); chandelier exit (LeBeau, textbook); Kaminski & Lo 2014 J. Financial Markets
ideas.review: Claims match our exit study (winners peak +1.92R and close +1.53R, only 2% reach +3R; breakeven-after-1R was rejected). The proposal did not say which ATR; fixed below as the ATR(14) at the signal close, the same one our stops use. S2 is switched off in the main account now, but its paper record (every signal) measures the new exit either way.
ideas.where: Backtest first (exit-study rule, then the 36-start account test). If it passes and you approve: S2 in the main paper account; the live check uses S2's paper record of every signal, so it does not wait for the account to take trades.
ideas.backtest_rule: S2 keeps its entry, its 2xATR first stop and its 20-session limit; the 4xATR target is removed. Trail = max(first stop, highest close since entry - 3 x ATR(14) at the signal close), updated at each close and used from the next session (live: the 15-minute checks sell at market at or below it). Pass: on 2024-2025 at least +0.05R per trade better than the current S2 exits, then 36 starts (40/60, $300 + $250/month, 24 months) better in >= 60% of starts, median gain > 0, median worst drop no more than 1 point deeper; 2026 reported.
ideas.live_check: Every S2 paper trade from the day it is switched on is followed both ways on the same signal: new trailing exit and old target exit.
ideas.removal_rule: After 30 closed trades: removed if new-minus-old R per trade has its 90% range entirely below 0. Early removal after 10 closed trades if the average is below -0.25R and its 90% range is entirely below 0.

ideas.title: Scale in on confirmation (all short-term rules)
ideas.source: Stanley's idea (2026-11-23): buy a small part first, add if the move continues; known as pyramiding / scaling in (e.g. the Turtle rules add units as a trade moves in its favour)
ideas.review: Adding only on confirmation (price moves our way), never averaging down. The stop never moves (moving it to breakeven was rejected in the exit study), and the add is sized so the most a trade can lose stays exactly the normal 1R of a full position. Trade-off: smaller losses on false starts vs smaller, later-bought winners and more orders.
ideas.where: Backtest first. If it passes and you approve: S2, S3 and S4 in the main paper account (not long-term L1, not the monthly experiments).
ideas.backtest_rule: Menu fixed 2026-11-23 before any result: start with fraction f of the normal size, f in {1/3, 1/2, 2/3}; add once at the next open after a close at or above entry + k x R (R = entry - first stop), k in {0.5, 1.0, 1.5}, only while the trade is open, not on a day the trade exits at the open, and not if that open is at or below the stop; the add's size a = (1 - f) / (1 + k) of the normal size, so the most the trade can lose stays 1R; stop, target, time limit and exit signal unchanged; 0.1% round-trip cost on each part. Profit per trade is measured in R of a full-size position. Step 1: on S2+S3+S4 signals 2015-2023 (design), pick the variant with the highest average profit per trade. Step 2: on 2024-2025 (check) it must beat buying the full size at once by at least +0.05R per trade; otherwise rejected. Step 3: 36 quarterly starts Apr 2015 - Jan 2024, 24 months, $300 + $250/month, 40/60, today's rules otherwise: better in >= 60% of starts, median gain > 0, median worst drop no more than 1 point deeper. Step 4: 2026 reported, and must not trail today's rules by more than 1 point.
ideas.live_check: Every S2/S3/S4 paper trade from the day it is switched on is followed both ways on the same signal: scaled in and all at once.
ideas.removal_rule: After 30 closed trades: removed if scaled-minus-all-at-once profit per trade (in full-size R) has its 90% range entirely below 0. Early removal after 10 closed trades if the average is below -0.25R and its 90% range is entirely below 0.
ideas.backtest_result: Step 1 (2015-2023, 1,940 trades): all 9 variants earned less per trade than all-at-once (+0.112R); best was start 2/3, add at +0.5R: +0.084R. Step 2 (2024-2025, 435 trades): best variant -0.046R per trade vs all-at-once (90% range -0.071 to -0.022R); needed +0.05R or better: FAILED, steps 3-4 not run. 2026: +0.075R vs +0.088R. Why: on trades that confirmed, the starter earned +0.8 to +1.3R per full-size unit but the add only +0.07 to +0.10R (it lost money 35-40% of the time): most of each move happens before the confirmation, so starting smaller gives up the best part. Files: research/scale_in_study.py, research/results/scale_in_steps12.*

decisions.by: Stanley: 'It adds risks, but it also has rewards, we just have to find the balance'

decisions.what: rejected by its fixed backtest rule (step 2)

ideas.title: Big-dip rebound (D1), a new short-term rule
ideas.source: Stanley's question about NVIDIA's -47% fall and +31% day (2026-11-23); my count of 401 past cases
ideas.review: Descriptive count before this test (2015-2025, 77 stocks): after a stock first closed 30%+ below its 60-day high it was up 20 sessions later in 75% of cases (median +10.3%), but a third of the cases were the 2020 crash, 26% fell another 10%+ first, and the 77 are today's survivors. Honesty note: the 30%/60-day trigger was picked after seeing those 2015-2025 numbers, so the 2024-2025 check is not fully clean; 2026 is.
ideas.where: Backtest first. If it passes and you approve: a new setup D1 in the main paper account's short-term bucket.
ideas.backtest_rule: Fixed 2026-11-23 before any result. D1, short-term, the 77 traded stocks. Signal at a close: close <= 70% of the highest close of the last 60 sessions, and the previous close was above that level (first day across). Entry next open; stop 2.5 x ATR(14) at the signal close; no target; time exit at the close of the 20th session; no exit signal. Usual sizing, earnings skip, per-setup switch and every other rule as for S1-S4. Step 1: the standard setup evidence bar used for S1-S4 (backtest 2015-2025, held-out from 2024: >= 30 trades, >= 5 years, positive held-out, Edge >= 2), giving its tier. Step 2: 36 quarterly starts Apr 2015 - Jan 2024, 24 months, $300 + $250/month, 40/60: today's rules plus D1 vs today's rules: better in >= 60% of starts, median gain > 0, median worst drop no more than 1 point deeper. Step 3: Jan-Nov 2026 must not trail today's rules by more than 1 point.
ideas.live_check: Every D1 paper signal (all 77 stocks) from the day it is switched on, followed with its own exits; compared with its backtest average R.
ideas.removal_rule: After 30 closed D1 paper trades: removed if its average R is more than 2 standard errors below its backtest average. Early removal after 10 if the average is below -0.5R. (The per-setup switch also pauses it whenever its last 20 average below 0R.)
ideas.backtest_result: Step 1 PASSED: 244 trades 2015-2025, +0.31R per trade, held-out +0.49R (45 trades), loss rate 37%, 1 in 20 trades worse than -17%, Edge 5, Confidence 4, Tier 3. Step 2 FAILED: today's rules + D1 better in 22% of 36 starts, median -1.29 pts, worst drop -2.65 pts deeper. 2026: +2.47 pts (reported). Why: signals cluster in crashes (81 in 2020, 67 in 2022); with limited cash the account takes the first ones, early in the fall, so D1's own account trades lost money in 67% of runs (median -$19.50), and those losses switched on the goal pause, which then blocked S2 (example start 2019-10: pause 334 days vs 193; S2 +$612 without D1, -$8 with it). Files: research/big_dip_study.py, results/big_dip_*.

ideas.title: Sector cap for the momentum experiment
ideas.source: Stanley's question (2026-11-23): 8 of the 10 momentum picks were chip stocks
ideas.review: Sectors are today's GICS sectors (research/sector_cap_study.py), applied to the whole history: a small bias, since some companies changed sector.
ideas.where: Backtest first. If it passes and you approve: the momentum experiment's own paper account (not the main account).
ideas.backtest_rule: Fixed 2026-11-23 before any result. Momentum as running (top 10 of the 77 by 12-1 month return, 10% each, monthly), but at most 3 of the 10 from one GICS sector: walk down the ranking and skip a stock whose sector already has 3. Compared with uncapped momentum, whole account in the strategy (0/100), 36 quarterly starts Apr 2015 - Jan 2024, 24 months, $300 + $250/month, 0.1% round trip, idle cash in BIL as in the tournament. Pass if EITHER (a) better than uncapped in >= 60% of starts, median gain > 0 and median worst drop no more than 1 point deeper, OR (b) median worst drop at least 1 point shallower and median gain no more than 1 point lower. Jan-Nov 2026 reported.
ideas.live_check: The uncapped ranking is kept on paper every month next to the capped holdings.
ideas.removal_rule: Reviewed with the experiment itself (it is a labelled experiment, not a live rule): removed if after 6 monthly rebalances the capped account trails the uncapped paper ranking by more than the 5th percentile of 6-month gaps in the backtest.
ideas.backtest_result: PASSED by rule (b): per start, worst drop +1.74 pts shallower (median), gain -0.48 pts (median), better in 47% of 36 starts; rule (a) not met. Medians of each: capped +26.2% / worst -22.0%, uncapped +23.2% / -22.2%. Jan-Nov 2026: gain -0.66 pts, worst drop +20.7 pts shallower. Files: research/sector_cap_study.py, results/sector_cap_*.
